s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital cerebral and ocular abnormalities with prenatal and postnatal findings
salient_findings: Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
key_facts: Born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
Weight at birth was 2152 g
One of monochorionic diamniotic twins
Identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI revealed microcephaly and marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles
No signs of elevated intracranial pressure
Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
Temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions
Family history was noncontributory
Weak light reflexes bilaterally at 1 week of age
Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign

shortlist.label: Walker-Warburg syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital muscular dystrophy, ocular malformations, and brain abnormalities, matching the patient's microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and optic nerve pallor

shortlist.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with congenital muscular dystrophy, ocular abnormalities, and brain malformations, consistent with the patient's prenatal and postnatal findings

shortlist.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Involves congenital muscular dystrophy, brain malformations, and ocular abnormalities, aligning with the patient's clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by a smooth brain surface due to defective neuronal migration, which could explain the patient's microcephaly and ventricular enlargement

shortlist.label: Septo-optic dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Involves optic nerve hypoplasia, pituitary abnormalities, and midline brain defects, consistent with the patient's weak light reflexes and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign

raw.rationale: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the ocular findings of weak light reflexes and mild optic nerve pallor, are consistent with Walker-Warburg syndrome, a disorder characterized by brain and eye malformations.

rejected.label: Muscle-eye-brain disease
rejected.why: While it shares some similarities with Walker-Warburg syndrome, the vignette lacks specific mention of muscular dystrophy or significant eye abnormalities beyond weak light reflexes and optic nerve pallor.

rejected.label: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy
rejected.why: The primary features of this condition, such as significant muscular dystrophy and intellectual disability, are not prominently described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Lissencephaly
rejected.why: Although lissencephaly involves brain malformations, the specific combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and the described ocular findings in the vignette better align with Walker-Warburg syndrome.

rejected.label: Septo-optic dysplasia
rejected.why: This condition primarily involves optic nerve hypoplasia, pituitary abnormalities, and midline brain defects, which do not fully match the broad range of cerebral and ocular abnormalities described in the vignette.
